newsitem.title: USA: U.S. check cashers group studies national network.
newsitem.headline: U.S. check cashers group studies national network.

text.p: A trade group representing businesses that cash checks for a fee said Thursday it is exploring "options and opportunities" including a national network to process U.S. government payments.

The National Check Cashers Association (NaCCA) said the committee is evaluating regional proposals being developed in response to a U.S. initiative which will require all federal payments except for Internal Revenue Service tax refunds to be issued electronically by 1999.

A NaCCA press release said the options under study include the creation of a national check casher network for electronic payments, including a repository for federal payments, by chartering its own bank, credit union or other non-bank financial institution.
An alternative would be development of a parternship or alliance with an existing bank or non-bank financial institution, the group said.

Earlier this week, the Check Cashers Association of New York and other plaintiffs won a victory in the New York State Supreme Court when judge Vincent Bradley ruled that the bidding process was flawed when Citicorp won a contract with the New York Department of Social services to provide electronic disbursement of benefits. The ruling nullified Citicorp's contract.
Transactive Corp, a unit of GTECH Holdings Corp, was also a plaintiff in the New York case.
